audit_findings.title: The earnings claim is stale relative to the 2026 denominator and balance sheet
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2024 OE anchor is projected against June 2026 shares and cash, although FY2025 and first-half 2026 operating results are available.
audit_findings.evidence: Our consolidated income from continuing operations before income taxes in 2024 was $473 million, compared with $260 million in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, not hypothetical. FY2025 operating cash flow less capital expenditures was $329 million, and the same unnormalized calculation was $253 million for the first half of 2026, versus the $78.4 million FY2024 anchor. These are not substitutes for consistently calculated OE, but they show that omitted periods contain changes large enough to alter the valuation materially. The direction remains unknown until identical normalization rules are applied.
audit_findings.action: Calculate FY2025 and trailing-twelve-month June 2026 OE under the original worksheet rules, reconcile it to the filed cash-flow statements, and rerun with shares and bridge balances from the same measurement date.

audit_findings.title: Working-capital investment appears absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $194 million 2024 cash use, equal to 247.4% of the $78.4 million anchor; 2025 cash use was $45 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring working-capital requirement is an additional investment deducted from OE before growth and terminal-value projection.
audit_findings.evidence: These items were partially offset by: (i) the impact of operating assets and liabilities utilizing $194 million of cash in 2024, compared with utilizing $99 million in 2023 and (ii) higher gains on sales of property and equipment of $35 million in 2024 compared with 2023, that is subtracted in the determination of operating cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The $194 million cash use is filed, but its omission from the worksheet and its recurring portion are unresolved because the detailed OE reconciliation is absent. Its scale exceeds the entire anchor, while the decline to $45 million in 2025 shows material timing variability. If a recurring requirement was omitted, the anchor and every projected period are overstated; even a minority of the 2024 amount would be significant relative to $78.4 million.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor line by line to operating cash flow, identify whether working-capital movements were already captured, separate recurring operating requirements from timing and growth effects, and rerun using the supported recurring amount.

audit_findings.title: A one-time tax benefit may be embedded in the recurring anchor and double-counted in cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $41 million, equal to 52.3% of the $78.4 million anchor; cash-bridge duplication unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring tax benefit would inflate normalized OE, while any related refund retained in June 2026 cash would also enter the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: During the second quarter of 2024, the Company executed a legal entity reorganization in our European Transportation business that resulted in a one-time tax benefit of $ 41 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $41 million benefit was one-time. It does not establish whether the valuation removed it or how much of the related refund remained in the $298 million June 2026 cash balance. XPO received a $49 million refund in 2025 and reported another $6 million expected in 2026 or 2027. Inclusion in recurring OE would be material by itself; simultaneous recognition through the cash bridge would double-count the same tax event.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $41 million benefit through the OE worksheet, trace the $49 million refund and remaining $6 million through cash balances, exclude the benefit from normalized OE, and rerun while recognizing the refund only once.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring real-estate gain appears to remain in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $34 million, equal to 43.4% of the $78.4 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in the anchor, the disposal gain is treated as recurring freight earnings and compounded through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The year-over-year increase primarily reflects $34 million in gains on real estate transactions in our North American LTL segment in 2024 from a planned service center relocation with no comparable gains in 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The $34 million nonrecurring LTL real-estate gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE is unresolved without the worksheet. The consolidated cash-flow statement subtracts property-sale gains from operating cash flow, so an OE calculation beginning with operating cash flow may already remove it; a net-income-based calculation may not. At 43.4% of the anchor, unresolved inclusion is plainly capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Identify the anchor's starting measure, verify that the full property-sale gain was removed exactly once, keep disposal proceeds outside recurring OE, and rerun if any gain remains.

audit_findings.title: Accounting pension income may be treated as recurring operating earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $25 million, equal to 31.9% of the $78.4 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Noncash pension income retained in normalized OE is projected as recurring distributable cash despite being driven by actuarial expected returns.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2024, our expected return on plan assets was $98 million, compared to the actual return on plan assets of $17 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates $25 million of 2024 pension income, including a $98 million expected return on plan assets versus a $17 million actual return. Whether the valuation retained that income is unresolved. The plans are frozen and produced only $6 million of accounting income in 2025, while 2026 estimated income was $14 million, confirming that the 2024 amount is not a stable operating run rate. Inclusion would materially inflate the anchor and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE reconciliation for the $25 million pension income, replace accounting income with supported company cash contributions or withdrawals after considering the funded and unfunded plans, and rerun the valuation.
